MAY 30 DILG BAGONG PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City v.æm_dilq.qov _ ph 72 HON. JOSELITO F. FIGURACION Municipal Councilor Sangguniang Bayan of Nabua, Camarines Sur Dear Hon. Figuracion: This has reference to the letter dated I March 2024 requesting for a legal opinion based on the Memoranda issued by Hon. Femando D. Simbulan, the Municipal Mayor of Nabua, Camarines Sur. You maintain the following representations, to wit: The Municipal Mayor issued several memoranda with noteworthy provisions such as: (I) the requirement of personal appearance of applicant before the Local Chief Executive/Approving Authority; (2) permission from the Local Chief Executive which must be personally applied from him with respect to application for leave, vacation, forced leave, sick leave; and (3) scope of the coverage of Memorandum dated 21 February 2024. You maintain that the following directives regarding personal appearance runs contrary to existing laws, rules and regulations in so far as it violates the basic rights of govemment employees and elected officials as well as their right to travel as enshrined in the 1987 Constitution. We discuss. Please be informed at the outset that this Department's duty is to implement the Local Govemment Code via, inter alia, the rendition of legal opinions. Legal opinions for that matter are executive constructions given by the govemment agency concemed on a particular view it is tasked to implement. However, legal opinions have limitations, such that they cannot be rendered on issues that require factual adjudication in view of some conflicting claimsl. Moreover, we are bound by this Departments Memorandum Order No. 2010-022 dated 17 September 2010 which provides that the Department shall not act on queries of the following kinds, to wit: (I) Those containing facts that are justiciable in nature. Justiciable issues are those that require adjudication by the courts of law as to who between the opposing parties have the better right over a given controversy; (2) Those presumptively valid acts, e.g., enacted ordinances, consummated acts that already enjoy the presumption of regularity on the part of the public officer concerned, and similar instances; DILG LO No. 24 s. 2005 2 Supplement to Memorandum Order No. 2010-01 dated 4 March 2010. "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

(3) Those that are litis pendencia or pending litigation, except when the court itself requests for the opinion. In the event that an opinion has been rendered by the Department and its field officers without knowledge or information that a case involving the issues raised in the query is pending in court, such opinion shall automatically be deemed ineffective; and (4) Those that are cognizable by other agencies of the govemment. Notwithstanding, for purposes of academic discussion, we cite the pertinent provision applicable in this case. SECTION 47. Approval of Leaves of Absence. - (a) Leaves of absence of local elective officials shall be approved as follows: (1) Leaves of absence of the governor and the Mayor of a highly urbanized city or an independent component city shall be approved by the President or his duly authorized representative; (2) Leaves of absence of a vice-govemor or a city or municipal vice-mayor shall be approved by the local chief executive concerned: Provided, That the leaves of absence of the members of the Sanggunian and its employees shall be approved by the vice- governor or city or municipal vice mayor concemed; (3) Leaves of absence of the component city or municipal Mayor shall be approved by the govemor; and (4) Leaves of absence of a Punong Barangay shall be approved by the city or municipal mayor: Provided, That leaves of absence of Sangguniang Barangay members shall be approved by the Punong Barangay. (b) Whenever the application for leave of absence hereinabove specified is not acted upon within five (5) working days after receipt thereof, thereof, the application for leave of absence shall be deemed approved A cursory reading of the provision would reveal that the law did not intend personal appearance of the applicant before the local chief executive or his/her approving authority. Nowhere in the provision would show that it must be personally applied with the local chief executive/approving authority with respect to application for leave, vacation, forced leave, sick leave. In fact, the minimum requirement is that a written permission from the concemed authority be obtained before proceeding with any local/foreign or personal/official travel. Notwithstanding, this opinion shall be without prejudice to any contrary opinion rendered by more competent authorities and/or the courts. We hope to have assisted you on the matter. Thank you very much. Very truly yours, BY ATTY. J Und OUSE Copy ORITY OF THE SEC OR R. LLAMAS ARY: etary for Extemal, Legal and Legislative Affairs ULLLS-LRALLD/sbl ished: ATV. ARNALDO E.
